newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Iranian speaker dismisses German court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Iranian speaker dismisses German court ruling.

text.p: The speaker of the Iranian parliament, Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri dismissed as "political" a German court finding on Thursday that Iran ordered contract killings in Berlin, saying it was untrue and demanding evidence.

"This accusation is not true," he told reporters on the first day of a visit to Moscow. "We have asked the German leadership many times if there is any evidence and if so to present it to us. But until now they haven't. The trial had a political tinge."

Nateq-Nouri, a leading candidate in next month's presidential elections, was speaking in Farsi translated into Russian by an Iranian translator after meeting the speaker of the Russian lower house, Gennady Seleznyov.
The Berlin court said Iran's Committee for Special Operations ordered the slaying of a group of Iranian Kurdish leaders in a Berlin restaurant in 1992.
The court said the Committee's members were the state president, the country's religious leader, the Ministry of Intelligence and other security officials.
Nateq-Nouri is due to meet President Boris Yeltsin tomorrow.
